title: The four-dimensional Chamon code
abstract: Fracton models have attracted considerable interest as candidates for quantum memories because of their unconventional ground-state degeneracy (GSD) and restricted-mobility excitations. The four-dimensional (4D) Chamon code introduced in our previous work is constructed via the 4D XYZ product of two two-dimensional (2D) toric codes. Its GSD grows exponentially with the system size, similar to that of the three-dimensional (3D) Chamon code, suggesting that it may be regarded as a 4D generalization of the 3D Chamon code. However, the excitation properties of the 4D Chamon code have not been studied in depth, and a high-performance decoding strategy is still lacking. In this work, we first establish the correspondence between the algebraic structure of the 4D Chamon code and the 4D lattice, thereby characterizing the geometric distributions of qubits and stabilizers. Second, we show that the 4D Chamon code supports three types of restricted-mobility excitations analogous to those of the 3D Chamon code, further supporting its interpretation as a 4D generalization of the 3D Chamon code. Finally, we uncover two structural properties relevant to decoding: a hyperplane symmetry and a projection-induced 2D toric-code structure. By exploiting these properties, we develop a two-layer decoding strategy that decomposes the original decoding problem into multiple independent and parallelizable subproblems. Numerical simulations show that the proposed decoder substantially outperforms BP-OSD in decoding accuracy, demonstrating the benefit of incorporating the intrinsic geometric and algebraic structures of the code into decoder design.
summary: This paper analyzes the 4D Chamon code, a complex quantum error-correcting code, confirming its structure and restricted-mobility excitations. The authors introduce a novel, efficient two-layer decoding strategy that leverages the code's underlying symmetries. This new decoder significantly outperforms state-of-the-art methods in numerical simulations, advancing the practical application of topological quantum memory.
main_problem: To characterize the 4D Chamon code, confirm its status as a 4D generalization of the 3D code, and develop a high-performance decoding strategy.
main_result: The paper develops a novel two-layer decoding strategy that exploits the code's intrinsic symmetries, achieving substantially better decoding accuracy than existing methods like BP-OSD.
method: The authors establish the code's algebraic structure, analyze its restricted-mobility excitations, and then decompose the complex decoding problem into multiple independent, parallelizable 2D toric-code-like subproblems.
model_or_system: The system is the 4D Chamon code, a type of fracton model constructed via the 4D XYZ product of two 2D toric codes, defined on a 4D periodic lattice.
key_observables: Ground-State Degeneracy (GSD), restricted-mobility excitations (monopoles and dipoles), and the logical error rate during decoding.
important_parameters: The dimensionality (4D), the type of noise (Pauli Z errors), and the comparison metric (decoding accuracy vs. BP-OSD).
main_assumptions: The core decoding strategy relies on separating the error components, particularly the mixed-face error ($\mathbf{e}_{	ext{mix}}$), which allows the problem to decompose into independent 2D subproblems.
figures_summary: Figure 9 compares the logical error rates of the proposed two-layer decoder against BP-OSD for 4D Chamon codes under pure Pauli Z noise, showing superior performance for the new decoder.
paper_structure: The paper first characterizes the code and its excitations, confirming its 4D generalization status. It then develops the decoding theory by identifying structural symmetries, leading to the proposal of a two-layer decoding algorithm that solves the projected equation first, followed by parallel decoding on the remaining components.
why_interesting: The work provides a concrete, advanced example of applying deep structural insights (hyperplane symmetry, projection) to improve quantum error correction decoding, which is highly relevant to building fault-tolerant quantum hardware.
